utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have the appearances, starting with the Prosecution. They seem to be rather alone today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's obviously correct, Mr. President. For the Prosecution, Ekkehard Withopf and Kimberley Fleming, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence; they are complete, in full number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Defence of Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, myself; and as defender and co-counsel, Mr. Bourgon, and Mirna Milanovic as the legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. Good morning, Mr. President. We have Rodney Dixon, Mr. Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and our legal assistant, Mr. Nermin Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber would like to say good afternoon to all those present. The Prosecution, Defence, and the accused. Before we start with the witness, the Chamber will make an oral ruling with respect to the matter raised two days ago, concerning an answer given by one of the witnesses. I should like to remind you that the question raised by the Defence on the 12th of January was about the following, now, whether a witness and not an expert witness can testify with regard to his opinion. This question was raised by the Defence, and it also had to do with the questions raised by the Judges as to jurisdiction. In view of Article 85(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which has to do with the presentation of evidence, and that is the title of the Rule, provides the following: That a Judge can ask witnesses any questions they deem fit at any stage of the trial. Rule 89, however, provides for the following: That the Chamber may admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value. Therefore, in a more general manner, the right to ask questions -- for the Judges to ask questions may be taken within their general mission to discover the truth. Of course, it is of interest to note, on the other hand, that the Judges of the Tribunal are professional judges, and they therefore are not restricted by national rules which would be applicable to a jury. And from that point of view, Rule 89(A) of the Rules of Procedure state that a Chamber shall apply the Rules of Evidence set forth in this section and shall not be bound by national Rules of Evidence. Therefore, combining all these rulings, the right of Judges to ask questions is a broad-based one and should not be restricted or limited in any way. The judge, therefore, has full authority to ask any questions he deems useful to arrive at the truth. Probative-value questions in respect to witnesses' answers is something that will be regulated and given weight to by the Chamber, and they will of course take into account all the different elements -- credibility, viability, and all the rest. Having said that, with respect to this particular case and the question raised on the 12th of January, our ruling is the following: The witness was heard in the case during an examination-in-chief and for a cross-examination, and in that case, the witness said that his -- that her husband was going to meet responsible persons from the BiH command in Mehurici in order to -- and he was asked whether the Mujahedin were a part -- find out whether the Mujahedin were a part. During the examination, it was indicated that the Muslim army, who were the ones who shot at them -- whether they were the ones who shot at them at Miletici. And the witness had also stated that some of the soldiers were wearing camouflage uniforms, T-1324. During the cross-examination, the Defence itself asked the witness whether their Muslim neighbours were members of the BiH army, and the witness's answer was in the affirmative, and that is at 31340. Now, the question that was raised, in view of the transcript in LiveNote - in French, not in English and I'm come back to that later on - so the question was as follows:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "According to you, Madam, the people who attacked your village - and you said that they were Mujahedin - would you say, in your opinion - of course, you're not a military expert - but you saw what happened because you were an eyewitness - do you think those foreigners, in your opinion, and to the best of your knowledge, were part of the BH Army or not?" And the witness gave the following answer:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I think that they did belong to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They were with the Muslims." Now, the next question was as follows:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "So that is what you think. But without any further elements?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Yes, that's right. They were with the Muslims, so I thought that they were together. I cannot say with any degree of certainty anything else, because I don't know about that." Now, the next question was:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In your opinion, therefore, the local Muslims were integrated in the BiH; is that right?" Answer:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Yes." Now, in view of these questions and answers, during the examination conducted by the Prosecution and the cross-examination by the Defence, and in view of the questions raised by the Judges themselves, the question did not have to do with the witness's opinion but on the knowledge that the witness had, based on a summary of what she said. So the question that was asked at no point in the French transcript reflected the opinion of the witness. So all necessary precautions were taken. Reference was made to what the witness had seen, because the witness was an eyewitness, and the knowledge that the witness had, and it was -- the witness was clearly asked to confirm what she had said in this particular case. So the question was formulated after the witness had provided elements on the basis of which it was able to -- we were able to assess her testimony, which will aid the Chamber until due course to give probative value to this testimony and decide what weight to give to it. Whatever the case, the Trial Chamber has the right to ask any questions that it considers to be useful, in order to determine the probative weight which is appropriate to any answer provided by the witness in the course of the examination-in-chief and in the course of the cross-examination. Having said that, and outside the scope of oral 1/9:15 decision, the Trial Chamber determined that the English transcript could have given rise, could have provoked the Defence to react as it did, because in English interpretation, the question that was posed was: "In your opinion." That was the English version. And I think that in such a case, the Defence believed that the witness had been asked for the witness's opinion, whereas in the French interpretation, no reference was made to an opinion of any kind that the witness may have held. So I think that this is what caused the Defence to react as it did. It was the English version which mentioned "In your opinion," -- the wording of which was "In your opinion," whereas in the French, these words were never used. In addition, if the Defence has time to consult the Robert and Collins French-English dictionary to check the semantics with regard to this matter of opinion, the Defence will see that an opinion can mean either a judgement, a conviction or an idea. This is page 617. Page 1.616 of the English version, "opinion", defined by Anglicists, can be an opinion or consideration. So opinion can be a point of view. The famous Concise Oxford Dictionary says the following with regard to the term "opinion": It can be a view or judgement, most necessarily based on fact or knowledge. And this means that, on the other hand, one could deduct that an opinion may be based on fact or knowledge. This is not excluded, as far as the Petit Robert is concerned; page 1536, an opinion could be a matter of judgement or someone's state of mind. On the other hand, as far as knowledge is concerned in the Petit Robert, this knowledge has to do with a fact or a manner of knowing, and the opposite of the term "knowledge" would be "doubt," or "ignorance." Having provided these semantic explanations, the Trial Chamber believes that it is not necessary to redact the witness's response, the response that the witness gave to the question posed to the witness. The Trial Chamber considers that it was the English translation which was misleading. Having said this, we will proceed, and I think that we have to go into closed session, because the Prosecution has certain details to provide us with regard to the witness. So, Mr. Usher, could we please go into closed session, in order to allow the Prosecution to expose their point of view, and so that the numerous people in the public gallery are not in a position to hear what is being said.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the measures taken will prevent the public from seeing the witness entering, but the public and the media will hear a distorted voice and see the image of the witness, which will be distorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will resume with the hearing, having applied the measures we have mentioned. Witness, can you hear the interpretation? Apparently you can't. I'll ask you this again: Witness, can you hear the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hear it now. I hear it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat that? Can you repeat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hear it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness, for your request. You have been granted protective measures. A pseudonym will be used. Your pseudonym will be XA while you're testifying. There will be voice distortion, so your voice can't be identified. And as far as your face is concerned, technical measures have been taken to prevent anyone from identifying you. In addition, your testimony can't be disclosed to anyone outside this courtroom. Have you understood what I have said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you are now going to take the solemn declaration, and the usher, who is by your side, is going to show you a text which you should read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You can sit down now. Witness, you're appearing for the Prosecution and you will be testifying about facts that you have witnessed. Your testimony will contribute to determining the truth, and you have to testify about what you have witnessed directly and not about things that you might infer. The Prosecution, that is, to your right, will be asking you a series of questions. After they have finished asking you their questions, the Defence for the accused, who are on your left, will also ask you some questions. If necessary, and if the Judges who are before you believe it is necessary to ask you any additional questions in order to clarify certain issues, we will do so. If a question is not clear, ask the person who has asked you that question to rephrase it, to ask the question again. Take your time to answer the question and try to avoid answering by yes or not to the extent that this is possible. Have you understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can now proceed with the examination-in-chief. The Prosecution may take the floor for its examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Withopf:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, and in the course of this examination, I will always address you as "Witness XA." Witness XA, can you please inform the Trial Chamber whether you have been a member of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but I think it would be appropriate, and I think this is the proper procedure, for the witness to write down his name, which will remain under seal, so that we know who the witness XA is. I apologise for having interrupted my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you'll be shown a piece of paper. You'll write down your first and last name on this piece of paper, and your date of birth. This piece of paper will be recorded. The registrar will make a record of it, and this is in order to be sure of your identity. The usher will show you this piece of paper, and please write down your first and last name and your date of birth and your address. And if you have a profession, could you make a note of it too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to thank the Defence for having pointed out this issue. Madam Usher, you will show this document to the Prosecution, first of all, so that they can confirm that this is in fact the right witness, that no mistake has been made as far as their witness is concerned. Is that the person? You will now show the document to the Defence so that they can check it. And show the document to the accused. Very well. Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit number will be P33, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P33, under seal. The Prosecution may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, you just informed the Trial Chamber that you have been a member of the JNA. Can you please provide us some more detail as to when you joined the JNA and as to when you left the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I joined the JNA on the 15th of January, 1989, and I returned in 1990. I was in Nis, and after that I was at the Bulgarian border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please tell the Trial Chamber where you grew up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I was born in Zenica. I grew up in the village of Janjac, near Zenica. It's eight kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to the transcript, Witness XA, can you please add as to at what time you left the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: On the 15th of January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there's a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client can't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the accused can't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Antonetti, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll ask the usher to check the technical problem, to the extent that she is capable of doing so. It concerns the interpretation from French into the B/C/S. If there is a problem, the best solution would be perhaps for the accused to move forward into the seat in front. Perhaps that equipment is working. Can you hear now? Everything all right? It seems that things are back to normal. Very well. Please continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, in light of the fact that there has been a technical problem, I restart my examination-in-chief. Witness XA, can you please inform the Trial Chamber whether you have been a member of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I was a member of the JNA from the 15th of January, 1989, which is when I went to the JNA, and I was stationed in Nis. Afterwards I was transferred to the Yugoslav Bulgarian border. And I left the JNA on the 15th of January, 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where you grew up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I grew up in the village of Janjac, near Zenica, and I was born in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Janjac, can you please inform the Trial Chamber what was the predominant ethnicity of the villagers in 1992 and the beginning of 1993 of that village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: In my village, the village of Janjac, there were only Croats living there. Just Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The villagers surrounding your village, Janjac, what was the predominant ethnicity of the villagers living in these villages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Most of them were Muslims. That was the majority population. And there was one Serb village. Its name was Osunjca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please provide us with the names of the predominant Muslim villages you were just referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. Those villages were called Lokvine, Kozarci, Obrenovci, and Stranjani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe the relationship between the Croats in your village and the Muslims in the villages you were just detailing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The relationship was -- actually, could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe was the relationship in 1992, in mid-1992, between the villagers, the Croat villagers, in the village you grew up, and the villagers in the villages, in the Muslim villages surrounding Janjac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: At that time, relations began to be strained, and on the hills - we can see the hills above our village - we could see armed people, mostly they had hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to seeing such people with rifles, how would you describe the relationship?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Before that, the relations were very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What caused this change in the relations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The change in relations was caused by the arming that went on. Everyone, on all sides, each man would keep to himself. There weren't that many contacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time, Witness XA, when you joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform us as to when you joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I joined the HVO in November 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which unit have you been a member of when you joined the HVO in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The Jure Francetic Brigade was my unit, and the brigade commander was Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber where the Jure Francetic Brigade was located, was based.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The Jure Francetic Brigade was based in a village named Podbrijezje, near Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November 1992, and later on, in the beginning of 1993, can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to which military units were on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: On the opposite side were the units of the BH Army, and they were the 7th Muslim Brigade, the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, and -- well, I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade, where was the 7th Muslim Brigade based, end of 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade was based at Bilmiste in the barracks there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bilmiste, is it part of any bigger town, or is it in the vicinity of any bigger town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Bilmiste is in Zenica. It's actually a district of Zenica itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of armament, was there a difference between the unit you were a member of and the ABiH units you were just detailing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Those brigades had many more soldiers, and weapons too. All the weapons were from the former JNA, and they came to possess those weapons, that is to say, the Muslim armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time, Witness XA, when you have seen foreigners in the area of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I noticed some foreigners. They spoke a different language. They had insignia in Arabic. They wore long beards and black bands. And sometimes I saw them with some sabres, and they were about 50 centimeters long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a particular word you referred to to these foreigners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: We called those foreigners the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, when was the first time you've seen such Mujahedin in the area of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The first time I saw those foreigners in the area of Zenica was the end of 1992. They were walking round town, quite normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they walking around the town of Zenica with the arms you just described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness XA, where these Mujahedin came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I know that they spoke Arabic and that they had Arabic writing on their flags. I think that they were from Afghanistan, Pakistan too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're making reference to Arabic writing on their flags. Did these Mujahedin -- end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993 -- carry such flags with them openly in Zenica and the area of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. They carried the flags around Zenica quite openly, and in Zenica too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness XA, where these Mujahedin were based at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: At the time, they were stationed in the village of Mehurici, of the Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time, Witness XA, when you joined the military police of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I did join the military police of the HVO, and that was at the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform us where the military police unit which you became a member of end of 1992/beginning of 1993 was based.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: That unit of the military police was based -- actually, it belonged to the Jure Francetic Brigade, and it was based in the Rudar Hotel in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Witness XA, when the relations between the HVO and the ABiH became even worse than at the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Relations deteriorated from one day to the next, and relations were worst when Zivko Totic, the commander of the brigade, was captured and his escort killed on the road near Podbrijezje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still recall, Witness XA, when your commander, Zivko Totic, was kidnapped and his escort were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that, because I was there on the spot, and that was on the 11th of April, 1993, in the morning, between 8.00 and 9.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please inform us where the location Podbrijezje, as you just mentioned, is located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Podbrijezje is located near the town of Zenica. It is about five kilometres away, or three to four kilometres away from Zenica. And nearby is the steelworks of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were saying, Witness XA, that the escort of Zivko Totic was killed. Can you please inform us of whom the escort was comprised of.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The escorts to Zivko Totic were his brother, Ljubomir Totic, and his brother's son, and his name was Mladen Jandric. The driver was there. He was also killed. Yes, I forgot that, and I've forgotten his name. And there was another man who was hitchhiking, so they took him in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get to know that other people, in addition to Zivko Totic's escort, have been killed in the course of this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of that incident, a couple, an elderly couple, were also killed. They were between the ages of 50 and 60. And when I arrived on the spot where Zivko was captured and where his escorts were killed, that elderly couple was lying down on the ground some 50 metres away from the actual spot that Zivko Totic was captured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber in which capacity you visited the scene of the crime.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: As I've already said, I was a military policeman of the Jure Francetic Brigade, and Zivko Totic was the brigade commander. So from the headquarters, from the command at Podbrijezje, we were informed of what had happened and told that we had to go on the spot immediately. And when we arrived there, all the people were already dead. I wasn't able to recognise anyone, because their heads had been shattered. They were shot at from a distance of about five metres, that is to say, close up. And there were about a hundred cartridge cases lying around, an M-84 millimetre type of machine-gun. So we set up a barrier there, and the representatives of the HVO arrived in due course, and so did the representatives of the BH Army, as well as the HDZ and SDA representatives, because at the time, the HDZ and the SDA were the two ruling parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, you were just saying that representatives of the ABiH arrived at the spot. Can you please provide us some more detail in that respect.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The representatives of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, together with representatives of the HVO, conducted a scene-of-crime investigation, and we, the military policemen, were standing at a distance of about 100 metres from the actual event. Later on, they went to the Croatian centre in Zenica. They had a meeting of some kind there. Probably they didn't manage to reach an agreement, because things were worse afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Things were worse afterwards," just quoting your last few words. What does it actually mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: That means that on the 17th of April, that is to say, five days after Zivko had been captured, and we were all in the hotel, all of us, and when the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade entered the Croatian centre and broke everything that was there, there were two of our men there who were on guard, and they came to tell us that the place had been stormed by members of the 7th Muslim Brigade and that, quite simply, they forced them out. And two hours later, they shot at the hotel, so that we had to withdraw from the hotel, to a village that was called Grm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification, Witness XA, the hotel you are referring to, is it the base of the HVO Jure Francetic military police unit? This is the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The hotel was the base of the Jure Francetic military police, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, did there come a time when you have been arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still recall the date as to when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I was arrested on the 21st, between the 21st and 22nd of April, 1993, in the apartment of -- I was arrested on the -- between the 21st and 22nd of April, in the apartment in Zenica, and the name of the street at the time was JNA Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber, Witness XA, as to who arrested you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I was arrested by the 7th Muslim Brigade, the military police of the 7th military brigade [as interpreted], in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know that it was the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: All of the people who turned up in the apartment where I was located had insignia denoting the 7th Muslim Brigade and its military police, and the people who were on the stairwell, and there were about ten of them, they also had patches of the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, I'm now going to show you a photo board showing a number of different military shoulder patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: This is the Prosecution Exhibit P5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This exhibit was tendered under the number of P5; is that right? It is Exhibit P5?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's completely correct, Mr. President. And I'm going to present the exhibit via Sanction to the Witness XA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, on this photo board, can you identify the shoulder patch -- can you identify one of the shoulder patches as being the one which has been worn by the members of the military unit which arrested you in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It's patch number 16. But that patch was straight at the top.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What does the witness mean when he says that it was straight at the top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the same patch as shown here, but it wasn't egg-shaped. It was straight at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you have been arrested on the 21st, 22nd of April, 1993, where did the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade did you bring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade took me off to the Music School, which was located near the central cinema in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, I'm now going to show you a photograph. It's the Prosecution Exhibit P8.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And since the witness -- since I will ask the witness at a later point in time to make some markings on it, the Prosecution has to present it and has to tender it in hard copy. It's the Prosecution's exhibit P8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have P7 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's exactly, Mr. President, Your Honours, the photograph I wish to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So, if I understand you, you have a copy to show the witness for him to authenticate it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's completely correct, Your Honour, Your Honours, and it's actually Exhibit P7. I apologise. Can the witness please be shown the photograph Exhibit P7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, if you have a copy already, perhaps you could show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: There is such a copy available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what you can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I can see on the photograph the Music School, and it was next to the central, or central cinema hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the Music School in Zenica you were just referring to that you have been brought to after you have been arrested by members of the military police of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. That's the Music School where I was taken to when they captured me, that is to say, when I was captured by the military police of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The time you were brought to the Zenica Music School you just identified on this photograph, where in this building were you brought to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: They took me to the cellar of this building. You can see the small windows by the road. That's where the cellar was located, which is where they took me, and I spent 15 days there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA --

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can the witness please be provided with a text marker. Can it also please be put on the ELMO, the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark with the text marker the windows of the room in which you were brought in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please write in the grey area beneath these windows, the words "this is the room I was detained."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, given that there are protective measures that have been granted, I think that this photograph should be relayed by the Internet system. If he writes something down on the photograph, his writing can be identified, and that could give rise to certain problems, to a slight problem. So if he doesn't mark anything, his name or any other details, this might be useful, since this document should be relayed to the exterior. We will take confidential measures later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Thank you very much. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please write down what I just mentioned: "This is the room I was kept in detention."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So no one can see what he has marked on the document. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President. That's the way it should be. And the photograph will later on be shown to Defence and the two accused, I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, I'm now going to show you a further photograph. This is Prosecution Exhibit, and I understand it's now P8. And again, we have the photograph available in hard copy as well. Witness XA, can you please inform the Trial Chamber what you can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I can see the room. When the police from the 7th Muslim Brigade brought me there, that's the room that they took me to, and that is where I spent 15 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification, Witness XA, is this the room from inside you just marked on the other photograph, with the access from outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the inside of the room that I -- the outside of which I have marked on the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day of your arrest, you were just informing the Trial Chamber, you were taken in this room. What happened to you after you were taken into this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: When they took me to this room, there was a door there. It only consisted of sort of rods, and then three policemen from the 7th Muslim Brigade appeared and they told me to approach the door and to put my hand through the sort of rails. They took everything that I had on me. They took my shoes off too, my ring, my watch, and the money I had on me. While I spent 15 days there, I was barefoot all the time. I had no shoes. Afterwards, about one hour later, some other people descended. There were five of them. When they started taking me out, up the stairs, I was hit with a wooden implement on the head, and then I lost consciousness. When I regained consciousness, I was in a room where there were between 15 to 20 of those policemen from the 7th Muslim Brigade. They interrogated me. They put some questions to me. They asked me how many Muslim women I had raped. They asked me which Croats had weapons, cars, rifles. They continued to beat me until I lost consciousness, and after a certain period of time, they threw me back into the cellar, into the basement. And this continued for about eight days, on a daily basis. Then they stopped beating me for a two-day period, but the policeman on duty, on the first floor, when their colleagues from the battlefield arrived, they would let them go into the basement to beat us again. So during that 15-day period, we were maltreated, beaten, et cetera. There were no toilet facilities. We didn't have any water. We had a gallon, which weighed about three kilos. And sometimes there would be up to 30 of us. And that was drinking water. In this photograph, you can see, to the right, there was a sort of bucket, five-litre bucket, and that's where we were able to relieve ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, you were just informing the Trial Chamber about the beatings. Can you go into more detail by what means, with the help of what tools, you have been beaten by the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Usually, these were wooden handles. We called them spade handles. Then they used rubber truncheons. They sometimes had knuckle-dusters. That's what we called them - either wooden or iron ones. They would kick us, they would beat us with whatever they could get their hands on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that these were members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade's military police which beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: All of these people -- most of them had the insignia of the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Those of them who didn't and who beat me are the ones who had arrived -- or would arrive from the battlefield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, we're going to have to stop, because an hour and a half has almost passed, and for technical reasons, in order to change the tape, we cannot continue. So you'll have to continue with your cross-examination. I'm going to ask Madam Usher to lower the blinds to prevent the witness from being seen. Naturally, we will take care of the two documents in a short while. Witness, we will now have a 25-minute break. You'll be able to rest in a room for witnesses, and we will resume the hearing after the break. That will be at 10 past 4.00. And as we will be working until 7.00, we will be having another break. We will now adjourn, and we will resume at 10 past 4.00 precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The protective measures are still in place. There is just a little correction that I would like to make. On the basis of the transcript, what will be redacted has to do with the details that concern the witness's identity, the details that would allow him to be identified. And what appears in the English transcript. Mr. Withopf, please continue with your examination-in-chief, and we have protective measures in place which are being controlled by Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, for the information of the Trial Chamber, you have described the beatings, and you have described the means by which members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Antonetti, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Defence inform us of whether we have a technical problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I have understood, the accused said that he can now hear the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution very well, but he has to strain to hear the witness's answer. But I think everything is fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you please say, number one, to see whether the accused can hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The witness can't hear. The accused has to be in a position to hear the witness's answers, but apparently we have a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've been told that the technician is arriving. If the problem continues, the best solution would be for Mr. Kubura to sit in front. Things should be functioning there. Could the usher check to see whether the system in front of the accused is working, though it's also necessary for there to be headphones there. The usher is going to check. Here's the technician. Could you say "one" again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently it's working now. The Trial Chamber would like to thank the technician. Mr. Withopf, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, for the information of the Trial Chamber, you were describing the beatings by the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade's military police in the Zenica Music School, and you were detailing beatings on your head. Can you please inform the Trial Chamber which other parts of your body have been affected by the beatings.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: They beat me all over my body, with the exception of my legs. It was mostly my back, the stomach, my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the beatings you were mentioning prior to the break caused you being unconscious. Was there any additional bodily harm inflicted by this beating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: As a result of these beatings, I was wounded. I had two cracks in my head. One was four to five centimetres wide, four to five centimetres long - you can still see it - and the other was a two-centimetre wound at the back of my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, you were just mentioning that one can still see the scar that has been caused by this beating. Can you please show to the Judges the scar on your head that has been the result of the beating that caused you being unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is prepared to show the participants of this trial the scar, and the witness -- whatever you wish -- can either come to the Judges's desk or whatever you think is the appropriate proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It won't be necessary for him to show everyone the scar, but he can use his finger to point to the location of his scar. We will trust him. Unless the Defence wants to see it for himself. Witness, please point to the scar on your head. Use your finger to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The scar is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Is this a problem for the Defence? Otherwise the Defence the approach the witness to check the scar. Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any medical treatment you got in the Zenica Music School after you had been hit on the head and this scar, or this wound, has been inflicted on your head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: This blow to my head was dealt to me on the first day, and the wound remained an open wound for the 15 days that I was there. No one treated me at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform us whether this wound, this open wound, was visible to the guards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: They were able to see the open wounds at all times, because it was bleeding all the time. They could see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which military unit the guards in the Zenica Music School were part of.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The guards in the Zenica Music School belonged to the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the beatings, the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, were there any threats from their side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. They did make threats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please detail which sort of threats.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: When I was supposed to leave the Music School, or rather, when they wanted to transfer me to the KPD, the correctional facility, then I had to go up to the first floor to be questioned, at which point their interrogator said that if I told anyone about what had happened, about everything that had happened, after having left Zenica, if I told anyone about anything that had happened, they said that they would find the most distant relatives of mine, my parents, and that wherever they were in the world, regardless of where they were in the world, he said that he would kill them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has there been any threat to kill you whilst you have been in the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: They threatened to kill me on several occasions. I remember one occasion when two Muslim policemen took me outside the Music School. I was given a pickaxe, and they told me to dig a hole in the ground, which I did for about half an hour. And then they started laughing and they said that I should dig deeper, because that was going to be my grave. They said it shouldn't be shallow; it should be a deep grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other detainee with you when you dug what has been said being your grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. There was another detainee with me. He was also digging another hole next to where I was, but it wasn't as large as the one I was digging. And afterwards, a little later on, they put some rubbish in that hole. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please, for the information of the Trial Chamber, describe the food conditions and the sanitary conditions in the Zenica Music School, the conditions for the detainees.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The first 40 hours, we weren't given anything to eat. The sanitary conditions were terrible. We slept on wooden sort of pallets, and in the left corner we had a container, five-litre container, which we used to relieve ourselves. To the right, there were four to five benches which we used to sleep. When someone came to the basement, at any time, three or four or 2.00 in the morning, we all had to sit and look down at the ground. We were never allowed to raise our heads. The sanitary conditions were very bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you haven't got anything to eat for the first 40 hours, what did you get to eat after the first 40 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Every time they gave us something to eat, it was actually a little bit of water with some rice in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it mean "every time they gave us something to eat"? Can you please go into some detail.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: After those two days, we were sometimes given meals twice a day, sometimes once a day, and it was always water and rice. That's what it was like until the end of my stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber how many other detainees were detained in the basement of the Zenica Music School during the time you have been a detainee in the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: When I arrived, there were roughly ten other detainees there, and every day the number of detainees changed. Sometimes -- actually, 25 to 30 was the highest number that I saw, and the least I saw was 10. But the detainees were never the same. Some would stay for three days, and you would never see them again; then they would bring in some other ones; and that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the ethnicity of the other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: While I was there, there were two Serb detainees, and all the rest were Croats.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly request that the microphone of the President be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were two Serb detainees, and all the rest of the detainees were Croats. The detainees, were they soldiers or were they civilians, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: As far as I could tell, most of them were soldiers, but there were some civilians too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, Witness XA, please provide us with some names of the other detainees?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And I would request the Trial Chamber to order to redact the respective portion of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Registrar, would you redact the names just cited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, in view of the fact that the public is able to hear, the people in the public gallery, these answers should be given in private session. So, Mr. Usher, having said that, may we go into private session, please. I know it's complicated, but we must all make an effort. And we'll have to see from one moment to the next.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, the other detainees, were they beaten as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. All of us there were beaten, some more, some less; but all of us were beaten, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all of you beaten by the same people, meaning members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, all of them were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bodily injuries inflicted on the other detainees, were they a similar scale? Were they of a similar scale as the ones you had to suffer from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: It depended. With some, they were on a similar scale; with others, less. But most of the people with me had serious bodily harm inflicted on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the serious bodily harm which was inflicted on other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: One of the detainees was injured in such a way that his left arm was fractured. I know his name. I forgot to mention it a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please avoid giving names at this point. Now, if you really want to give a name, we can go back into private session. So if you wish to substantiate an injury by giving a name, we can go into private session. So please tell us, warn us in advance, so that we can go back into private session. Please proceed, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I would suggest to go into private session to enable the witness to inform you about the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Private session again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These bodily injuries you were just detailing, were they either visible or were they known to the guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: All those bodily injuries were caused by those same guards, so everybody could see them. They were quite obvious and evident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the guards actually the very same persons who beat the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. They were guards too. Actually, they weren't guards; they were just the people who were on the first floor all the time, that is to say, the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade. That's who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving on to a different issue, Witness XA: Have you ever seen Mujahedin in the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: At the Zenica Music School, on the eighth day that I was there in the school, they didn't beat me on that particular day, and one of those policemen belonging to the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade arrived and told me to go upstairs, to the upper storey, to wash the toilets there. And the WC was to the left of the entrance. On the right-hand side there were three or four men who spoke Arabic, and they had long beards and rifles. And on the butts, there were some sort of scarves, and there were some Arabic writing on the scarves. And I think that they were the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This particular room in which you have seen the Mujahedin, was there any writing on the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: On the door of that room there was some writing, right at the top, and it was something written down in Arabic. And in the middle of the door, in the Latin script, it said "Hezbollah."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, what was your impression of this room? What purpose did this room, based on your impression, serve for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I saw the room. It was open. I saw bunk-beds. And there were some soldiers lying down on them in boots. Some of them were laughing. Their rifles were hung on the bed posts. I think it was a dormitory, which enough room to take 20 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of such Mujahedin have you seen in the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I just saw those three or four that day. I didn't see any more people speaking Arabic in the Music School. As to the other policemen who were there, they were speaking our own language, but they also had very long beards, so it was difficult to distinguish the Mujahedin from them, until they began speaking Arabic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually hear the individuals whom you describe as being Mujahedin speaking Arabic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. On that particular day, I did hear them speaking Arabic, and that's why I said that I had seen the Mujahedin, precisely because they were speaking Arabic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm now going to show the Witness XA, again, Prosecution Exhibit P5. That's the photo board with the shoulder patches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf. We must decide about the fate of the other exhibits which were placed on standby. If I remember correctly, the photograph showing the Music School building was one of them, and he can authenticate the photograph with his name. Now -- and that's what he did, I believe. So, Witness, you now have the photograph of the Music School. Could you place your name and date, today's date, on the photograph. You placed a cross on that photograph. Is that right, Mr. Withopf?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right, Mr. President, Your Honours. I wish to make the witness mark some additional markings at a later point of today's proceedings; therefore, if you could just, for a few minutes, postpone this procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you prefer to take the documents together. As you wish. Witness, keep the document beside you, and we'll decide on what we're going to do with it once the Prosecutor feels you don't need to go back to the documents. So you're going to show him another document now; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Your Honours, I'm going to show the witness the Prosecution Exhibit P5, which has been shown to the witness at an earlier point in time of today's proceedings. Can the witness please be shown the Prosecution Exhibit P5. It's on the screen, I understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, do you see the photo board with a number of different military shoulder patches in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please identify the one or the ones you've seen in the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: As I've already said, number 16 was the one I saw, as well as patch number 21. I saw that particular patch on the scarves and head scarves, but it wasn't quite like that. It said "Jihad," and it said something in Arabic. There was the star, the crescent, and a sabre on it. I didn't see any of the other patches in the Music School.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness XA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So number -- patch 21 does not quite correspond to the patch he actually saw, because he said there was an inscription on it, I think, but he said he saw he saw a sabre. So he says that it wasn't exactly the same as the patch on the photograph; at least on the basis of the interpretation I was given. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please, in some more detail, describe the difference between the patch you've seen on the photo board, or you see on the photo board in front of you, and the patch you've actually seen in the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: In the Zenica Music School, I saw the patch on the scarf and on the head scarves, on which it said "Jihad," as it says here on this patch, patch 21. It was exactly like that, except the shape was different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the difference in shape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: At the bottom, it was rectangular. Otherwise, everything else was the same. Everything else that it said on it was the same. But it wasn't a triangle; it was a rectangle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you have in front of you -- Witness XA, you have in front of you the photograph with the building which you identified as the Zenica Music School. Can you see on this photograph the room in which the Mujahedin were located within the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we have to follow the same procedures previously today in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark on this photograph the room in which the Mujahedin were located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can see it says on the English transcript here, the Prosecutor mentioned twice -- said they are located, and the interpretation we are receiving means where they were put up, accommodated. Now, the witness never spoke about the accommodation of the Mujahedin. He was talking about the room in which he saw the Mujahedin. So I don't think that the Prosecutor should rely on something that the witness didn't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps there's a problem of interpretation once again between B/C/S, English, and French. Of course, if everybody spoke French, there would be no problem, but as that is not the case, we have to deal with the situation. Mr. Withopf, would you ask your question again, bearing in mind the pertinent observation made by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you identify and mark on the photograph in front of you the room in which you have seen the Mujahedin during the time of your detention in the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark this room on the photograph in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the witness could place the photograph on the ELMO so that we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, unfortunately, I can't see whether you have already marked the room in which you have seen the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I have marked that room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please add a straight line from this marking to the grey area of the photograph and write down "this is the room in which I've seen the Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we're in open session, if we want to show the photograph, place it on the ELMO, we'll have to go into private session. Perhaps it's not necessary to show it at this point, so we can stay in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is the last marking I wanted the witness to draw on this photograph, and it can be now, please, be tendered into evidence, after the witness dated and signed it and it has been shown to Defence and the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you please put your name on the photograph, and today's date. And it is the 14th of January, 2004, today. That's the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, could you take the photograph and show it to the Prosecution so that they can check what has been noted. Please show it to the Defence, who will examine everything that has been written down very carefully. Show it to the accused, who will take their time to examine it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Judge Antonetti, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will have a look at it too. Could we have a number, an exhibit number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be P7.1, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to use this opportunity to also tender the second photograph, showing the basement of the Zenica Music School, into evidence, after the witness has dated and signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, as you did a minute ago, please mark your first and last name on this second photograph, and today's date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document will be shown to the Prosecution, then to the Defence, and to the accused. Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number, after having shown us the document in question.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be P8.1, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have remembered this correctly, he should have written something down. He wrote something down on a white piece of paper, and we haven't decided on what to do with this piece of paper yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, we have dealt with all the exhibits. Usher, could you just check to see that there are no other documents with the witness. There are no other documents, then. Mr. Withopf, would you like to proceed with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Zenica Music School, Witness XA, there were the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, as you informed the Trial Chamber about; there were the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade military police, as you informed the Trial Chamber about; and there were the Mujahedin, as you informed the Trial Chamber about. How would you describe --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we discussed this matter a minute ago, and we said that the Mujahedin weren't accommodated there. The witness said that he only saw them there on one occasion, and that was on the eighth day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's obviously a translation problem. I said nothing else that the Mujahedin were in the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but it's possible to be there in two modes. One can be passing through, one can be there on a temporary basis, or on a permanent basis. If you want your witness to provide you with details, do ask him some questions. But the Defence quite rightly pointed out that you cannot claim that its members were there at all times, all the time, because that is not what the witness said. You, therefore, have to ask the witness to provide more details about the situation, because, for the moment, we don't know what sort of situation these people were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, in the Zenica Music School, there were members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and there were members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade military police, and you have seen Mujahedin in the Zenica Music School. How would you describe the relation between the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade's military police, and the Mujahedin you have seen in the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The relations between the members of the military police of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the soldiers, and the Mujahedin that I saw there, relations were very close, and the soldiers of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Mujahedin members that I saw there, I think that they went to the battlefield together. But the Mujahedin were there on a temporary basis, I think. I only saw them on that occasion, and never again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that the witness said only what is stated in the last sentence, and he said that before: I saw them then, and never again. Everything else is no more than opinion and conclusions that have no grounds, and I think that the sort of question put to the witness by the Prosecution and this response are not in accordance with the Rules that should be followed when questioning an ordinary, factual witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could please respond. Defence counsel may later on cross-examine the witness on this issue, but this is not the right time to make a legal argument on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The essence of the question is whether the witness saw the people that he mentioned only occasionally, or whether it was on a permanent basis, and this is what the Defence has pointed out. So the witness should avoid inferences. Witness, you've been asked to say what you saw. What did you really see? What was the situation? Did you see there all the time, only temporarily, only occasionally? What did you actually see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw the Mujahedin on the eighth day. They spoke in the Arabic language. And after that, I never saw them in the Music School again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the witness has told us that he saw them on the eighth day and that after that day he did not see them again. Isn't that correct? Mr. Withopf, having clarified the matter, please continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, you mentioned several times that you have been interrogated. Do you still recall the name of the interrogator?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, the situation is identical. If he mentions the name, as we are in open session, he could be identified. So we will go into private session. Mr. Registrar, could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please carry on, Mr. Withopf, but keep an eye on the clock, because we still need time for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I'll do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were brought -- Witness XA, when you were brought to the Zenica Music School and you entered the Zenica Music School, did you see anything in written at the main entrance door of the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: At the entrance to the Music School in Zenica, the entrance door consisted of iron bars, and there was the inscription "the 7th Muslim Brigade" above the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything else written at the door or at the vicinity of the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Nothing else was written on the door, but nearby, as I have already said, to the right in that room, there was something in Arabic on the door that was written there, and it said "Hezbollah" in the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, can you please detail for the information of the Trial Chamber the proceedings prior to your transfer to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Before I was transferred to the KP Dom, on that night - it was perhaps 1.00 or 2.00 in the morning - then three men appeared. I think they were commanders, because they were wearing better uniforms than the others that were there. But they didn't have ranks of any kind. They said all the blood that I had on me should be washed and that I was going to be escorted by two policemen. I went up to the first floor. I washed the blood off, to the extent that this was possible, but it wasn't possible to wash it all off. So they sent me back on three occasions to wash all the blood off. I wasn't able to wash all of it off, but after an hour had passed, they put me in a bus and took me to the KP Dom in Zenica. It was a VW bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, the three men who were wearing better uniforms than the others and who didn't have any ranks of any kind, did they, however, have any military insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get to know at some point in time, Witness XA, who have been the three officers or the three individuals with the better military uniforms you were just talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Since we are in open session, the name that was mentioned could be means of identification. So, Mr. Registrar, it is necessary to delete this name from the audiotape. Things are proceeding so rapidly that it is only later that we notice that there is a problem. In line 19, 17:18:15 is the hour, it is necessary to delete this name from the audiotape. So have me sign an order to this effect. Please continue. We are still in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, if you have the very same concerns in the event the witness answers my last question, we should go back into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll go back into private session, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, do you still recall the date when you were actually transferred to the KP Dom in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I was transferred to the KP Dom in Zenica on the 5th of May, 1993. I stayed in the KP Dom until the 19th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Upon arrival at the KP Dom on the 5th of May, 1993 -- who brought you at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Members of the 7th Muslim Brigade took me to the KP Dom. They used a small VW bus to take me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who received you in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Members of the military police of the BH Army received me there. And when I arrived there, they told me I was lucky that I wasn't being put in solitary confinement. I was told that I would be with all the detainees, the HVO members who were already there, and there were between four and five hundred of them. They told me that I first had to wash all the blood off me, every drop of blood, that not a single drop of blood should be visible on me, and they said that they would then take me to the KP Dom, where all the other detainees were located. On the first day, they took me to wash myself. I then washed off the blood. And on the second day, members of the Red Cross came and registered me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification purposes, were the men who told you that you first had to wash all the blood off you, every drop a blood, that not a single drop of blood should be visible on you, were these the members of the military police of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The person who told me that I had to wash myself was a member of the BH Army military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, Witness XA, still have any visible wounds at the time you were transferred to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, I did still have visible wounds. But when the Red Cross registered me, they told the guards that I had to be provided with medical treatment immediately. A doctor arrived, and he helped me; he treated me.
