utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of doctor was it? Was it a civilian or a military doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: He was a civilian doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you finally being released from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I was released from the KP Dom on the 19th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, did you know at the time where the ABiH 3rd Corps headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The headquarters, at the time it was located in the Travnik Street, in the Institut.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecution please accelerate a bit, because we'll have to have the break soon. How much more time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I anticipate that I won't need more time than five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, do we have another five minutes at our disposal? We should have another five minutes. Good. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, you were just informing the Trial Chamber that the headquarters of the ABiH 3rd Corps at the time was located in the Travnik Street, in the Institut. How far is this location away from the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: It was not more than 800 metres from the Music School in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, did you know at the time where the headquarters of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The command of the 7th Muslim Brigade was in Milimiste [as interpreted], in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the transcript it says "Milimiste." Isn't -- can you please spell the name of the location where the 7th Muslim Brigade headquarters was located, or can you just repeat the name of the location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Bilmiste, B, Bilmiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XA, how far is this location, the command of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, away from the -- was it away from the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: About three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness XA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, this concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In order to allow the Defence counsel to proceed with their cross-examination, the Trial Chamber won't ask any questions, although we have a lot of questions. But it's necessary for the cross-examination to be completed. It is half past 5.00. We will have the pause, in accordance with the regulations, and we will resume at 5 to 6.00. And the Defence will have one hour and five minutes to carry out its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed at 5.55, which gives the Defence an hour for their cross-examination, without wasting any further time, I give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In order to protect confidentiality, I should like to have a ruling prepared, or rather, would the registrar please redact that from the transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have permission to say "XA"? In my language, there's a different word for witness in the masculine, and witness in the feminine. So when I say witness, I will have to use one or the other. But yes, I will do my best to call you "XA."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on other occasions, did you ever make statements, or to other organs, about what you have testified to today; and if so, would you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: You've already asked me. Yes, on one other occasion, but there were no other subsequent occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you to make a pause after hearing my question for my microphone to be switched off, so that your voice can't be picked up on my microphone. Thank you. Is it true and correct that in May and June 1992, in the immediate vicinity of your country, conflicts began with the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Conflicts with the Serb army, or rather, between them and the HVO, never occurred in my own village, but there were conflicts between the Serb village of Osojnica and the Muslim village of Ljubac [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did the inhabitants of your village organise themselves because they felt tension in your immediate environment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: The population did organise itself. Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, you had your own weapon; is that right, and you were armed with that weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I did not have my own weapon, but I was issued a Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the village, you organised patrols and village guards; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until November 1992, you did not belong, in formal terms, to any army, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: No, I did not belong to any army until that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Asked by my learned colleague of the Prosecution, you said that you joined the HVO in November 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the Jure Francetic Brigade, you and all the other members of that brigade had uniforms and weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: We didn't all have uniforms and weapons. At the time I joined up, when I joined the brigade, the Jure Francetic Brigade, one platoon numbered approximately 30 men. Of those 30 men, about 20 of them were armed and in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were transferred to the military police of that brigade, as a military policeman, you had authority over members of your own brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. Our authority was restricted to the members of our own brigade. However, we worked together with the members of the members of the military police of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina wherever there was a conflict between the Muslim units and our units, or where there were problems between the two ethnic groups. Then we would go to intervene together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that up until this event, when Zivko Totic was kidnapped -- that is to say, your commander -- you frequently went on patrol together and solved problems together with the military police of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The HVO had its own checkpoints at some of the exits from town, especially the ones in the direction of Ovnak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: What period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the spring of 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were on duty at the Rudarski Hotel, or miners' hotel, when you received information that Commander Zivko Totic had allegedly been killed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were on the spot to provide security, you learnt from eyewitnesses that Zivko Totic was taken off in a Mercedes kombi van; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: In a white kombi van, a Mercedes one, which had no windshield in front. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The van belonged to the Mujahedin, and they had been seen around driving the van previously; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. I would see them personally on occasion. Frequently, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Asked by the Prosecutor, you said that they would be seen in town from time to time. Now, I'm asking you the following: Is it true and correct that many inhabitants and members of the HVO and the army were rather afraid of the Mujahedin when they came across them in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is true too, that the members of other ethnic groups were also afraid of those Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were providing security at the crime scene, where Commander Totic was captured, you said that investigators from the army turned up, and from the civilian police, the MUP of Zenica, in fact; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I didn't say that the civilian police of the MUP of Zenica arrived. What I said was that members of the BH Army arrived on the spot, as did members of the HVO, and also members of the HDZ, the political party, and members of the other political party, the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to intervene for the same reason. I think that I'm going to give the floor first to Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I noticed on repeated occasions that my learned colleague is asking questions and making reference to "the army." Since there are different armies involved, I would like to ask my learned colleague to identify which army she is talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: (redacted). Witness XA, when I said "the army," when I say "the army," is it clear to you that I mean the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: To me, that was quite clear, that you meant the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army. But I'd like to ask you to say, to tell me whether you think that the 7th Muslim Brigade belonged to the BH Army, was it part of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to be able to answer your questions, so please accept this. On the 18th of April, is it true that you found yourself up at the front line, near a place called Grm? And I mean the time when the attack you mentioned was launched against the Croatian centre, or Dom. Is it true and correct that you received an order to withdraw to the Croatian village of Grm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Could you switch your microphone off, please. Thank you. That is correct, and that took place on the 18th of April. We withdrew to Grm, and once we arrived up there, it was about 5.00 a.m., and we were at the Zrnici house, houses. They were all Croatian houses, and they were ablaze when I got there. After that, we withdrew, following orders from Vinko Baresic, who replaced Zivko Totic, and we withdrew to Cajdras, which is where we stayed until about noon, until the Croatian houses were burning at Grm. And then Baresic said that we should all surrender, and that's what I did too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've answered another two or three questions that I had intended to ask you. So once you received the order to surrender, you went to your sister's house and changed until civilian clothing from your army uniform; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, five or six buses arrived, together with the military and civilian police, and they were supposed to drive you to the KP Dom, the correctional facility; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I might mention certain names in my next two questions, so may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you for taking that precaution. Mr. Registrar, may we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you stayed in that apartment until you were led off?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I was saying, is it true that you stayed in your friend's apartment until you were taken away to the Music School? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I stayed in that apartment until the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade came to fetch us, and that was during the night, at about 1.00 p.m., when they took me to the Music School. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you anything more of what you experienced in the Music School, because you've already explained that in great detail to the Court. All I would like to ask you is this: Is it true that the threats uttered, when they told you that you weren't allowed to tell anybody what had happened to you, did you take that to be a serious threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. I took it very seriously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the reason why you never told anyone while you were in Zenica of what you had experienced at the Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: That was one of the reasons, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day after you arrived in the KP Dom, you said that you were visited by the International Red Cross. Is it true that in Zenica you had some relatives too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I did have relatives there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true and correct that your aunt visited you and brought you a change of clothing, and that you were able to write to your relatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: My aunt did visit me. She brought me food and clothing. But I never wrote to any other relations, because I didn't know where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the KP Dom, you were also visited by the late - he is deceased today - he was the parish priest from Cajdras; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes. He visited all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were released from the KP Dom in June 1993, on the 19th of June, I believe, and were transferred to Vitez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you spoke about your difficult experience in the Music School for the first time to the investigator of the Tribunal; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the first time you spoke about your difficult experiences in the Music School was when you spoke to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the Kubura Defence like to ask any questions? I give them the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, we do have several questions for this witness, and may we move into private session, because we're going to mention certain names which could indicate the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, may we move into private session. Do the necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, I have two questions that concern the facts you have testified about. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These questions relate directly to what you did and saw. We do not know what your military rank was. You said that you were a policeman, a military policeman in the HVO. But were you an ordinary policeman or did you have a superior rank? What was your position? What was your rank.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: I didn't have a rank of any kind in the military police of the Jure Francetic Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. And my second question, which is a is he very simple one: When you were transferred to the KP Dom, when you arrived in this prison, did you sign, register an entry register; did they make you sign a register or did they just make you enter without your name being noted, without any supervision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: No, I didn't sign a register of any kind, not until two days later, when representatives of the Red Cross arrived. I wasn't assigned a number of any kind in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And when you left the KP Dom, were you asked to sign a document, a piece of paper, to put your name down in the register, or did you just leave without any other administrative procedures having been followed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: When I was leaving the KP Dom, I signed a statement which I had been given by the commanders in the KP Dom, and this statement stated that when I arrived in the musical school -- it said when I arrived in the musical school, when I left the musical school, when I arrived in the KP Dom, and when I left the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling us that you signed a piece of paper when you were released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Does the Prosecution have any additional questions to put to the witness? And if these questions contain any details that might permit the witness to be identified, tell us, so that we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has no further questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. Witness XA, the Trial Chamber would like to thank you for having testified here. You came here to testify for the Prosecution. You have testified and you have answered all the questions put to you. We wish you a good trip back. I'm going to ask the usher, who should first check that the blinds have been lowered before you leave the courtroom. We must pay attention to all the details, in spite of the fact that no one appears to be present in the public gallery. But it's best to follow this procedure. Witness XA, you will now be taken out of the courtroom, and I'd like to thank you again. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll go back into public session. The blinds need to be raised again, and we'll go back into public -- into open session again. But we need to raise the blinds. It would be best if the Presiding Judge could press a button to do this himself. It would be more rapid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll turn to Mr. Withopf again. We'll have a new witness tomorrow. Can you confirm that this -- can you make sure that the witness will be here and that there won't be any problems? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the situation is as follows: We have one witness available to testify tomorrow afternoon. That's the first one, which is scheduled for Thursday, 15 January 2004, on our witness schedule. The second witness named on this schedule is not available. There are some problems with the travel documents and he cannot be made available at this point in time. So we have one witness for tomorrow. We have one witness for Friday. The witness for Friday is exactly the one which is mentioned on our witness schedule. We anticipate the examination-in-chief of the witness which is scheduled for tomorrow lasting for about one hour and 30 minutes. If Your Honours think it would be helpful to continue afterwards with the witness who is scheduled for Friday, that can be made possible. At this stage, this is subject to changes, but I could give you some indication in the course of tomorrow morning, as I would do to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. Withopf, if your Friday witness, if you could bring your Friday witness here tomorrow, that would be good, but I don't know where this witness scheduled for Friday is. I don't know whether he's still on his way here. But that would be useful. The Trial Chamber understands that it's difficult to organise all of this, but naturally, there is nothing to prevent us from bringing the witness scheduled for Friday to the courtroom tomorrow, providing he is here. And I don't think the Defence would find this inconvenient, given that they have prepared themselves already, and this shouldn't present any particular problems. Given that we are well aware of the significant amount of work done by both parties. So if the witness could appear tomorrow, that would be good. So this means that the second witness scheduled for Thursday, if you can't reach that witness, this witness should be heard next week. That is how I have understood the situation. Unless the witness scheduled for Thursday appears on Friday. Mr. Withopf, could you provide us with some clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Tomorrow we will have the witness which is mentioned as the first one on the witness schedule for tomorrow. We will do everything possible to have the witness who is scheduled for Friday following the testimony of the first witness scheduled for tomorrow, immediately afterwards this schedule, but it depends on a number of issues that still have to be sorted out. I will inform both Your Honours and Defence in due time on this issue. The witness who is scheduled on the witness schedule as the second one for tomorrow, this witness is as it stands now, and this is again subject to change, as this one will be scheduled for Thursday. I think it's a Thursday, the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you will schedule him for the 5th of February. That's good. Very well. We have a few more minutes. Do we have any news concerning the archives? As you are well aware, the Trial Chamber is very concerned about this matter. Does the Defence have any new information or are we still on standby as far as this matter is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are still waiting. We are waiting for them to call us from the cabinet of the general secretary, Mr. Solana, but in spite of the fact that they said they will inform us, and we will provide you with the information in the course of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's better to call them -- to contact them yourselves rather than waiting for them to contact you. Mr. Bourgon is nodding. Very well. We're going to adjourn. I'd like to thank everyone present, and we'll meet again tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of January, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.43 p.m.,
